fatal_errors: The cited L10 result requires approximately 50 at.% Pt, whereas the proposed coequal Pt component in equiatomic FeCoNiMnCuPt would contain only about 16.7 at.% Pt; the evidence therefore does not establish that the proposed composition will order into L10.
Using 50 at.% Pt would violate the stated almost-equiatomic composition constraint.
The proposal does not reconstruct the Ti-induced fcc/C14 dual-phase intervention, phase-specific magnetic transitions, or coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general objective of increasing coercivity and offers a physically reasonable anisotropy-based alternative with a measurable mediator and explicit falsification threshold. E1 supports RTA-enhanced coercivity and Pt-enabled L10 ordering in a related FeCoNiMnCu system, but only at a highly non-equiatomic 50 at.% Pt composition. It therefore cannot directly support L10 formation in the proposed equiatomic six-component alloy. E2 concerns a high-entropy oxide and provides no material-specific support. Relative to the hidden target, the intervention, microstructure, mechanism, temperature conditions, and phase-resolved outcomes are absent. The experiment is reasonably discriminating, although inclusion of both unannealed Pt-bearing controls and annealed/unannealed composition-matched controls would better separate Pt addition from annealing effects.
